info.title: NthLayer Core API
info.description: Tier-1 reliability-critical HTTP API: verdict store, case management, manifest catalogue, heartbeats, component state. Workers and bench access the store exclusively through these endpoints. Verdicts are immutable after creation; outcome resolution writes a new verdict referencing the original as parent.

get.description: Returns 200 with a fixed payload as long as the ASGI app is running. Does not check store connectivity — for that, query any /verdicts route and rely on the 5xx contract.

post.description: Creates a new immutable verdict. The request body is either a raw verdict dict OR a CloudEvents v1.0 envelope (auto-detected by the presence of a top-level ``specversion`` field); envelopes are unwrapped before validation. Returns 422 ``invalid_json`` for malformed JSON, 400 ``envelope_invalid`` if an envelope cannot be unwrapped, and 422 ``verdict_invalid`` if the inner record fails required-field validation. Duplicate ids return 409 ``duplicate``. Verdicts are write-once; subsequent resolution must use POST /verdicts/{id}/outcome or POST /verdicts/{id}/override.

schema.description: anyOf rather than oneOf: the handler's auto-detect uses a non-discriminator sniff (presence of ``specversion``); an envelope payload may also nominally validate against Verdict due to ``additionalProperties: true``, so requiring exactly-one would produce false negatives.

400.description: ``envelope_invalid`` — CloudEvents envelope could not be unwrapped (missing specversion/type/source/id, or ``data`` is not a dict).

409.description: ``duplicate`` — verdict id already in the store.

422.description: ``invalid_json`` (malformed body / non-object) or ``verdict_invalid`` (inner record missing required fields: id, type, created_at). The envelope path carries an ``envelope_version`` field on the error body to let callers distinguish raw vs unwrapped.

500.description: ``internal_error`` — opaque store failure. Store/SQLite messages are never surfaced to the client (opensrm-9uow.1).

get.description: Returns an array of verdict records matching the supplied filters. All filters are optional; with no filters the store returns the most recent ``limit`` verdicts. Time filters use ISO-8601 timestamps.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Filter by service name (exact match).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by verdict type (e.g. slo_status, drift_signal, outcome_resolution).

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return.

422.description: ``invalid_parameter`` — query parameter rejected (e.g. non-integer or negative ``limit``).

get.description: Returns the single verdict record with the given id. Verdicts are immutable so the returned shape is stable across reads. Returns 404 if the id is unknown.

parameters.name: verdict_id
parameters.description: Unique verdict id.

404.description: No verdict with the given id.

500.description: Opaque internal_error from the store layer.

get.description: Returns the ancestors of a verdict by walking the ``parent_ids`` chain upward via the lineage index. The optional ``max_hops`` query parameter caps traversal depth (0 = unlimited).

parameters.name: verdict_id
parameters.description: Verdict id whose ancestors are wanted.

parameters.name: max_hops
parameters.description: Maximum hops to traverse. Omit (or set to 0) for unlimited.

200.description: Array of ancestor verdict records (possibly empty).

500.description: Opaque internal_error from the store layer.

get.description: Returns the descendants of a verdict by walking the lineage index downward (verdicts whose ``parent_ids`` transitively include this id).

parameters.name: verdict_id
parameters.description: Verdict id whose descendants are wanted.

200.description: Array of descendant verdict records (possibly empty).

500.description: Opaque internal_error from the store layer.

post.description: Creates a NEW verdict with ``type='outcome_resolution'`` and ``parent_ids=[original_id]``. The original verdict is never mutated — this is the v1.5 canonical resolution path. The new verdict id defaults to ``out-<original_id>`` if not supplied. Returns 404 if the original verdict does not exist; 409 ``duplicate`` if the synthesized outcome id is already taken.

parameters.name: verdict_id
parameters.description: Id of the original verdict being resolved.

id.description: Optional explicit id for the new outcome_resolution verdict. Defaults to ``out-<original_id>``.

pipeline_latency_ms.description: Optional end-to-end pipeline latency for telemetry.

409.description: ``duplicate`` — synthesized outcome verdict id is already in the store.

422.description: ``invalid_json`` — request body is not a valid JSON object.

post.description: Mutation-style override path (opensrm-jmy.18): mutates the original verdict's ``outcome`` field in place via CAS in ``Store.update_outcome``. The single exception to verdict immutability and the ONLY endpoint that writes back to an existing verdict. Intended for invocation by the override-adapter sidecar exclusively — the sidecar is the privacy boundary, so core trusts the wire (``pre_redacted=True``). The body's ``decision_id`` MUST match the path's ``verdict_id``; mismatch returns 400 ``decision_id_mismatch``. Returns 409 ``conflict`` if the verdict is already overridden.

parameters.name: verdict_id
parameters.description: Id of the verdict to override. Must match the body's decision_id.

decision_id.description: Verdict id being overridden. Must equal the path verdict_id.

timestamp.description: tz-aware ISO-8601 timestamp of the override event.

actor.description: Operator identifier (already redacted by the sidecar).

reason.description: Operator-supplied rationale (already redacted by the sidecar).

409.description: ``conflict`` — CAS predicate rejected the write (verdict already overridden).

422.description: ``invalid_json`` (malformed body) or ``validation_error`` (override event failed construction — bad timestamp, missing required fields, or fallthrough from ``apply_override_to_verdict``).

500.description: Opaque internal_error from the store layer.

post.description: Persists an assessment record produced by a worker module (e.g. slo_status, drift_signal). Accepts either a CloudEvents v1.0 envelope (auto-detected via top-level ``specversion``) or a raw assessment dict. Returns 400 ``envelope_invalid`` when the envelope cannot be unwrapped, 422 ``assessment_invalid`` when the inner record is missing required fields, and 409 ``duplicate`` when the assessment id already exists.

409.description: An assessment with this id already exists.

get.description: Returns assessments matching the optional filters. Filters compose with AND semantics; omitted filters do not constrain the result set. The response is a JSON array ordered by the store's default ordering (newest first).

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Filter assessments by the service they apply to.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by assessment kind (e.g. slo_status, drift_signal).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of assessments to return.

post.description: Creates a new operator-facing case from an underlying verdict. Requires ``id``, ``kind``, ``created_at``, and ``underlying_verdict``. When ``priority`` is not supplied it is derived from ``blast_radius`` and ``has_active_incident`` (production+incident=P0, production=P1, staging+incident=P1, staging=P2, anything else=P3). Returns 409 ``duplicate`` when the case id already exists.

201.description: Case created. Response echoes id and final priority.

409.description: A case with this id already exists.

get.description: Returns cases matching the optional state, priority, and service filters. Used by the bench TUI to drive the operator queue. Filters compose with AND semantics.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter by case state (pending, leased, resolved).

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Filter by derived or explicit priority.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Filter cases by the service they concern.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of cases to return.

get.summary: Fetch a single case by id
get.description: Returns the full case record including lease state and resolution metadata if any. Responds 404 ``not_found`` for unknown ids.

parameters.name: case_id
parameters.description: The case identifier.

put.description: Atomically claims ownership of the case for the named holder until ``expires_at``. Exactly one concurrent caller succeeds; the loser receives 409 ``lease_conflict``. ``expires_at`` must be a future ISO-8601 timestamp (naive timestamps are treated as UTC). Returns 404 if the case does not exist.

parameters.name: case_id
parameters.description: The case identifier.

409.description: Case is already leased by another operator.

delete.description: Releases any lease currently held on the case — idempotent and intentionally admin-level (any caller may release; identity is not checked). Returns 200 whether or not a lease was held, and 404 only when the case itself does not exist.

parameters.name: case_id
parameters.description: The case identifier.

put.description: Atomically transitions the case to ``resolved`` while binding the supplied ``resolution_id`` (a verdict id) as the closing decision. The store guards against double-resolve: a second attempt returns 409 ``already_resolved`` with the previously bound resolution id.

parameters.name: case_id
parameters.description: The case identifier.

resolution_id.description: Verdict id representing the resolution decision.

post.description: Creates a named window during which automated responses are blocked. The body must include name, declared_by, declared_at, active_from, and active_until; active_until must strictly follow active_from. Duplicate names return 409.

409.description: A change freeze with this name already exists.

422.description: Missing required fields or invalid temporal ordering.

get.description: Returns the set of change freezes that are currently active according to their active_from / active_until window. Lifted freezes are excluded.

put.description: Cancels an active change freeze before its scheduled active_until. The body must include lifted_by. Returns 404 if no freeze with that name exists.

parameters.name: freeze_name
parameters.description: Name of the change freeze to lift.

404.description: No change freeze with this name.

post.description: Workers POST a liveness signal identifying the component and instance. The optional state field records arbitrary worker-specific status. Always returns 200 on success.

get.description: Returns all known heartbeats with a derived health field. A component whose most recent heartbeat is older than the threshold (default 30 seconds, override via ?threshold=) is marked degraded.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Age in seconds beyond which a heartbeat is treated as degraded.

200.description: Array of heartbeats with health classification.

get.description: Returns every OpenSRM v2 service manifest currently loaded by the catalogue. Manifest authorship happens on disk — there is no POST /manifests endpoint.

post.description: Re-polls the catalogue source directory for added, removed, or changed manifest files and returns the list of services that changed. The path segment '-' is a literal sentinel chosen because no service is named '-'.

200.description: Reload completed; reports changed services and total count.

get.description: Returns the manifest for the named service from the in-memory catalogue. Returns 404 if no manifest with this service name is loaded.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Service name from the manifest's metadata.

404.description: No manifest with this service name is loaded.

post.description: Workers report verdicts they declined to act on (active incident, dedup window, hysteresis, etc.) so the suppression decisions are auditable. Required fields: component, reason, suppressed_verdict_id.

get.description: Returns suppression records filtered by component and/or creation time range. Default limit is 100; supply ?limit= to override.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Restrict to suppressions reported by this component.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: ISO-8601 lower bound on suppression timestamp.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: ISO-8601 upper bound on suppression timestamp.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return.

put.description: Workers PUT an opaque JSON state blob (cursor, hysteresis, dedup cache, etc.) after each cycle so they can resume after crash. The body shape is worker-defined; core treats it as opaque.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Component name identifying the worker.

get.description: Workers GET their previously-persisted state blob to resume from the last checkpoint. Returns 404 if no state has ever been written for this component.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Component name identifying the worker.

200.description: The opaque state blob previously persisted by the component.

404.description: No state recorded for this component.

get.description: Diagnostic endpoint for the respond worker: returns action_request verdicts older than the threshold (default 60 seconds, override via ?threshold=) that still have no corresponding case. A non-empty list signals a silent failure in case creation.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Age in seconds above which an unresolved action_request is considered stuck.

200.description: Count and list of stuck action_request verdicts.

error.description: Machine-readable error code. Handlers raise a fixed vocabulary of codes documented per-endpoint. The internal_error code is used when the store layer raises an unexpected exception (opensrm-9uow.1).

detail.description: Structured detail. Shape varies by error code and endpoint. Operators read structured server logs for the canonical diagnosis; clients use this for user-facing messages.

Verdict.description: Immutable verdict record. Additional implementation-specific fields are permitted (the store preserves the JSON blob verbatim).

type.description: Verdict type discriminator. Common values include ``slo_status``, ``drift_signal``, ``outcome_resolution``.

service.description: Service name this verdict pertains to.

parent_ids.description: Lineage parents. Populated on derived verdicts (e.g. outcome_resolution); null/absent on roots.

chain_depth.description: Depth in the lineage chain (0 = root).

outcome.description: Outcome metadata. Absent or null until resolution; mutated in place by POST /verdicts/{id}/override (the shape is defined by ``apply_override_to_verdict`` in nthlayer-common). No enum is enforced server-side.

outcome_status.description: Top-level outcome status, set on outcome_resolution verdicts created by POST /verdicts/{id}/outcome. Defaults to ``confirmed`` when the request body omits it; otherwise pass-through from the body. No enum is enforced server-side.

resolution.description: Operator-supplied resolution detail on outcome_resolution verdicts. Shape is caller-defined.

reasoning.description: Operator-supplied free-form reasoning on outcome_resolution verdicts.

pipeline_latency_ms.description: Optional pipeline-latency annotation. Pass-through from the outcome request body.

EventEnvelope.description: CloudEvents v1.0 envelope. POST /verdicts (and POST /assessments) auto-detect this shape via the top-level ``specversion`` field and unwrap before validating the inner record carried in ``data``.

id.description: Envelope id (independent of the inner record id).

Assessment.description: An assessment record produced by a worker module — a typed observation about a service's health (e.g. SLO status, drift signal). Inner shape varies by ``kind``; per-kind detail lives in the open-ended ``data`` field.

Case.description: An operator-facing investigation derived from an underlying verdict. Cases progress through ``pending`` → ``leased`` → ``resolved``. A lease names the operator currently working the case; ``null`` means no operator holds it.

priority.description: Derived from blast_radius × incident context if not explicitly supplied at creation.

has_active_incident.description: Whether an active incident was in flight at create time.

underlying_verdict.description: Verdict id that originated this case.

resolution_id.description: Verdict id bound when the case was resolved (resolved state only).

lease.description: Current lease, or null when unleased.

CaseLease.description: An exclusive claim by an operator on a case, bounded by an expiry timestamp. Acquired via PUT /cases/{id}/lease and released via DELETE on the same path.

holder.description: Operator identifier currently holding the lease.

expires_at.description: When the lease lapses if not refreshed.

CaseCreate.description: Request body for POST /cases. ``priority`` is optional — when omitted it is derived from ``blast_radius`` and ``has_active_incident``.

underlying_verdict.description: Verdict id that originated this case.

blast_radius.description: Deployment scope used for priority derivation.

has_active_incident.description: Incident context used for priority derivation.

expires_at.description: Future ISO-8601 timestamp at which the lease lapses. Naive timestamps are treated as UTC.

ChangeFreeze.description: A named window during which automated responses are blocked.

Heartbeat.description: Liveness signal from a worker component.

Manifest.description: An OpenSRM v2 service manifest loaded into the catalogue.

spec.description: The OpenSRM v2 manifest body, opaque to core.

Suppression.description: An operator- or worker-recorded 'ignore this verdict pattern' decision.

ComponentState.description: Opaque per-worker persistence blob used for crash recovery.

StuckActionRequest.description: An action_request verdict whose deadline elapsed without a response.
